result_text:
**Hold, unless the raw access logs are restored before the freeze. If they are, run the check and decide on that result.** Your own ranges don't settle ship versus hold, though, and the hold is a lean, not a certainty.

I worked only from the ledger and did not open the evidence files.

**What the evidence is worth**
- The ledger's only usable discriminating evidence is the reference class (T3). It shows the 40 ms gap in 9 of 10 real regressions and 2 of 10 non-regressions. That gives a likelihood ratio of 0.9 / 0.2 = **4.5** in favor of "real".
- The 10/10 split was set by the analyst, so it carries no base rate. That's fine for a likelihood ratio, but it means the reference class can't replace your prior.
- I used the ratio once. T1 (the 57 ms canary/control gap) and T3 are the same observation, so counting both would double-count.
- The ratio rests on 10 cases per group, so it is itself uncertain.
- The canary/control gap comes from the same pipeline that H2 (an exporter artifact) questions, so it can't rule out H2.

**Posterior odds that the regression is real**

| Prior (real : not) | Posterior odds | P(real) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1:50 | 0.09 | 8% |
| 1:20 | 0.23 | 18% |
| 1:10 | 0.45 | 31% |
| 1:5 | 0.90 | 47% |

**Decision rule**
Hold if (cost ratio) × (posterior odds) > 1. The cost ratio is how much more a missed regression costs than a one-week hold, so your 2–20 range sets the break-even odds at 1:2 to 1:20.

| Prior odds | Cost ratio 2 | 5 | 10 | 20 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1:50 | ship | ship | ship | hold |
| 1:10 | ship | hold | hold | hold |
| 1:5 | hold | hold | hold | hold |

- Shipping is right only in the optimistic corner: a low prior (about 1:9 or lower) combined with a low miss cost (about 2–5×).
- If I spread both ranges evenly on a log scale, hold wins in about 72% of the combinations. I made that weighting up; it is not data.
- The team's disagreement on the cost number and on the prior is what decides this, so that is the argument to have.

**What would change it**
- **Restore the raw logs (S3).** This is the only test that separates a real regression from an exporter artifact. It is worth chasing hard, because it replaces the whole table with a direct answer. Retention is 7 days and the restore is still pending, so confirm it's actually feasible.
- **Check the exporter config history on the canary hosts.** The ledger's H2 prediction includes a config diff, and that may not need the raw logs.
- **If you hold, agree in advance on what releases it.** For example, flat raw-log p95 on the canary hosts means ship the next week.

The ledger dates the release as 2026-09-12, which is a Saturday. I assumed the "Friday" freeze means the day before.
